tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.

Weigh 100 mg sample in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min, repeat shake/hold once if not dissolved; stepwise add 0.9 mL, 2 mL, 7 mL solvent (same shake and hold) to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved use 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble) then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble. Repeat with alcohol.
Test 1 (zinc): dissolve 0.1 g in 5 mL water; add 0.2 mL strong sodium hydroxide solution; a white precipitate is formed.

details.reference: USP Identification Tests-General <191>, Chemical Identification Tests, Zinc

tests.procedure: Test 2 (sulfate): with barium chloride TS, solutions of sulfates yield a white precipitate that is insoluble in hydrochloric acid and in nitric acid.

details.reference: USP Identification Tests-General <191>, Chemical Identification Tests, Sulfate

tests.procedure: Lead limit test (USP <251> Procedure 1, chemical method): standard = 5 mL water, 0.50 mL standard lead solution (10 ppm) and 10 mL potassium cyanide solution (1 in 10) in a comparison tube; test = 0.25 g zinc sulfate in 5 mL water with 10 mL potassium cyanide solution (1 in 10), allowed to clear; add 0.1 mL sodium sulfide TS to each, stand 5 min, view downward over white surface. Sample not darker than standard (NMT 20 ppm).

Arsenic limit test (USP <211> Procedure 1, colorimetry): standard = 3.0 mL standard arsenic solution diluted to 35 mL; test = portion equivalent to 215 mg zinc sulfate in 35 mL water; add 20 mL 7 N sulfuric acid, 2 mL potassium iodide TS, 0.5 mL stronger acid stannous chloride TS and 1 mL isopropyl alcohol; stand 30 min; generate hydrogen with 3.0 g granular zinc for 45 min into silver diethyldithiocarbamate TS. Any red colour from the test does not exceed the standard (NMT 14 ppm); if needed read absorbance at 535-540 nm.

Alkalies and alkaline earths (gravimetric): dissolve the equivalent of 1.12 g zinc sulfate in 150 mL water in a 200-mL volumetric flask; precipitate zinc completely with ammonium sulfide TS; dilute to volume; filter through a dry filter and reject the first portion. To 100 mL of the filtrate add a few drops of sulfuric acid, evaporate to dryness in a tared dish, ignite to constant weight. Residue NMT 5 mg (0.9%).

details.reference: USP 2022 Monograph for Zinc Sulfate Monohydrate

tests.procedure: Acidity: sample solution equivalent to 28 mg/mL zinc sulfate; the sample solution is not coloured pink by methyl orange TS.

details.reference: USP 2022 Monograph for Zinc Sulfate Monohydrate

tests.procedure: Assay (complexometric titration): sample equivalent to 170 mg zinc sulfate (ZnSO4); dissolve in 100 mL water; add 5 mL ammonia-ammonium chloride buffer TS and 50 mg Eriochrome black TS; titrate with 0.05 M edetate disodium VS to deep blue. 1 mL of 0.05 M edetate disodium = 8.072 mg ZnSO4. Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100) / Wt.

details.equivalenceFactor: 1 mL of 0.05 M edetate disodium = 8.072 mg ZnSO4
details.formula: Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100) / Wt; E.P = end point (mL); eq.wt = equivalent weight of zinc sulfate monohydrate; F = titrant factor; Wt = sample weight (g)
details.titrantStandardization: about 200 mg standard calcium carbonate, 2 mL diluted hydrochloric acid, hydroxy naphthol blue titration with 0.05 M edetate disodium; M = (g CaCO3 x Assay/100 x 1000) / (100.09 x mL EDTA)
details.reference: USP 2022 Monograph for Zinc Sulfate Monohydrate
details.basis: as stated (no basis word on the STM)

tests.procedure: Test 3 (reactions of sulfates, BP): Use 5 mL of solution S; add 1 mL of dilute hydrochloric acid and 1 mL of barium chloride solution R1; a white precipitate is formed.

details.solutionS: 2.5 g in carbon dioxide-free water diluted to 50 mL
details.reference: BP Appendix VI Qualitative Reactions and Tests, Sulfate

tests.procedure: Test 4 (reaction of zinc, BP): Use 5 mL of the prescribed solution; add 0.2 mL of strong sodium hydroxide solution (a white precipitate is formed); add further 2 mL strong sodium hydroxide solution (precipitate dissolves); add 10 mL ammonium chloride solution (remains clear); add 0.1 mL sodium sulfide solution; a flocculent white precipitate is formed.

details.reference: BP Appendix VI Qualitative Reactions and Tests, Zinc

tests.procedure: Appearance of solution (BP): Compare Solution S with water. Solution S is clear and colourless.

details.solutionS: 2.5 g in carbon dioxide-free water diluted to 50 mL
details.reference: BP Appendix IV A & IV B

tests.procedure: pH (BP): Determine on Solution S using a calibrated pH meter.

details.solutionS: 2.5 g in carbon dioxide-free water diluted to 50 mL

tests.procedure: Chlorides limit test (BP): Sample = 3.3 mL of solution S diluted to 15 mL with water, add 1 mL dilute nitric acid, pour into 1 mL silver nitrate solution R2. Standard = 10 mL chloride standard solution (5 ppm Cl) and 5 mL water, add 1 mL dilute nitric acid, pour into 1 mL silver nitrate solution R2. Stand 5 min protected from light. Any opalescence in test not more intense than standard (maximum 300 ppm).

details.reference: BP Appendix VII Limit Tests, Chloride

tests.procedure: Iron limit test (BP): Sample = 2 mL solution S diluted to 10 mL with water, add 2 mL of 200 g/L citric acid monohydrate and 0.1 mL thioglycolic acid, make alkaline with ammonia, dilute to 20 mL with water. Standard = 10 mL iron standard solution (1 ppm Fe), add 2 mL citric acid and 0.1 mL thioglycolic acid, make alkaline with ammonia, dilute to 20 mL with water. After 5 min, any pink colour in test not more intense than standard (maximum 100 ppm).

details.reference: BP Appendix VII Limit Tests, Iron

tests.procedure: Assay (complexometric titration, BP): Dissolve 0.160 g in 5 mL dilute acetic acid, dilute to 200 mL with water. Add ~50 mg xylenol orange triturate and hexamethylenetetramine until violet-pink, add 2 g hexamethylenetetramine in excess. Titrate with 0.1 M sodium edetate until yellow. 1 mL of 0.1 M sodium edetate = 17.95 mg ZnSO4,H2O. Calculation: Assay = (E.P * eq.wt * F * 100) / Wt.

details.solvent: 5 mL dilute acetic acid diluted to 200 mL with water
details.equivalenceFactor: 1 mL of 0.1 M sodium edetate = 17.95 mg ZnSO4,H2O
details.titrantStandardization: 0.120 g zinc dissolved in 4 mL HCl R1, dilute NaOH to weakly acid, xylenol orange triturate, hexamethylenetetramine, titrate with 0.1 M sodium edetate to yellow
details.reference: BP 2024 Monograph for Zinc Sulfate Monohydrate
details.basis: as stated (no basis word on the STM)
